q: In Micah 5:12, the Hebrew word kesheph means:
opts: A type of harvest festival
Sorcery or witchcraft
A city in Israel
A musical instrument
explain: Kesheph is the plain Hebrew word for sorcery or witchcraft. It is the exact practice God says He will remove. (Strong's Hebrew H3785, BibleHub)

q: True or False: Saying “the blood of Jesus” over and over, like a magic phrase, is what makes Revelation 12:11 work.
explain: False. David Guzik's commentary on Revelation 12:11 warns against treating the blood of Jesus like a magic word. Victory rests on the real, historical fact of Christ's finished sacrifice — not on how many times you say it.

q: Numbers 23:23 says: “Surely there is no ______ against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel.”
explain: “Enchantment” (Hebrew nachash) — this is Balaam's own admission that no spell has power over God's people.

q: Who spoke Numbers 23:23, and in what situation?
opts: Moses, blessing the people before his death
Balaam, forced by God to bless Israel instead of cursing them
Joshua, before the battle of Jericho
David, before facing Goliath
explain: Balak, the king of Moab, hired Balaam to curse Israel. But God made Balaam speak a blessing instead — a public admission that no magic could touch God's people.

q: Match each scripture to its main point.

pairs.right: God removes witchcraft completely from His people
No spell can work against those in covenant with God
Real victory comes through Christ's blood, honest testimony, and courage
Christ's blood speaks a better word than Abel's blood

explain: Each scripture answers a different part of witchcraft's threat: removal, protection, victory, and a better word than judgment.

q: Put these steps of the prophetic direction in the correct order.
items: Pour the blood of Jesus on the earth
Rest the outcome in God's hands
explain: The direction moves from the act of faith, through the specific declarations, to the sealing prayer, and ends in rest — not repeated anxious action.

q: A believer keeps losing job opportunities right before the final decision. A friend says, “Just say the prayers every day and don't bother applying anywhere else.” What is the more biblical response?
opts: Only pray, and stop applying for jobs
Only keep applying, and skip prayer entirely
Pray about the spiritual pattern, and also keep applying and preparing well
Avoid job interviews altogether to be safe
explain: The biblical pattern joins prayer with wisdom and hard work — not superstition, avoidance, or magic words. Deal with the spiritual root in prayer, and also take practical steps.

q: True or False: Pouring liquid on the ground is what gives this prophetic direction its power.
explain: False. Every scripture behind this direction — Hebrews 12:24 and Revelation 12:11 — points to what Christ's blood already did at the cross. Pouring it out is your act of faith in that finished work. It is not a ritual with power of its own.

q: According to Hebrews 12:24, whose blood does Christ's blood “speak better” than?
opts: Abraham's
Moses'
Abel's
David's
explain: Hebrews 12:24 says Christ's blood “speaketh better things than that of Abel.” Abel's blood cried out for vengeance (Genesis 4:10). Christ's blood speaks forgiveness and welcome instead.

q: Revelation 12:11 says believers overcame “by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their ______.”
explain: “Testimony” (Greek martyria) — believers' own honest, spoken account of what God has done.

q: A family member keeps saying discouraging things right before you attempt something important. What is the balanced response?
opts: Say nothing and cut them off completely without ever talking to them
Pray Prayer 3 privately, and also set a calm, honest boundary in the relationship
Say the exact same discouraging things back to them
Ignore it completely and never mention it or pray about it
explain: Prayer 3 deals with the spiritual root. Proverbs 18:21 shows why words carry weight. Pairing prayer with a calm, honest boundary is the balanced response — not silence, getting back at them, or cutting them off without ever talking.

q: In your own words, explain why treating “the blood of Jesus” as a magic phrase would misunderstand Revelation 12:11. Write a sentence or two, then reveal a model answer.
model: Because the verse's victory rests on the real, historical fact of Christ's finished sacrifice — believed and spoken honestly — not on saying a sentence a certain number of times. Treating it like a chant would turn faith in a person (Jesus) into superstition about a formula.
